item.title: In Iraq, ISIS members once jailed in Syria face trial
item.description: In Iraq, NPR attends trials of French ISIS suspects after transfer from Syrian camps.
item.content:encoded: In Iraq, NPR attends trials of French ISIS suspects after transfer from Syrian camps.

item.title: Barbara Kingsolver's book 'Partita' grapples with the reality that our bodies fail us
item.description: Partita follows a young Appalachian woman with the chops to make it as a classical pianist. It was somewhat inspired by Barbara Kingsolver's love of classical music and her restrictive hand condition.
item.content:encoded: Partita follows a young Appalachian woman with the chops to make it as a classical pianist. It was somewhat inspired by Barbara Kingsolver's love of classical music and her restrictive hand condition.

item.title: Supreme Court case centers on battle over liability for climate change harms
item.description: The Supreme Court heard its first argument of the new term: a case about how much power local governments have to recover the costs of responding to the effects of climate change.
item.content:encoded: The Supreme Court heard its first argument of the new term: a case about how much power local governments have to recover the costs of responding to the effects of climate change.

item.title: New report details airstrike on Iranian school
item.description: NPR's Sacha Pfeiffer speaks with Jeremy Scahill of Drop Site News, which has issued an extensive new report on the U.S. airstrikes on a school in southern Iran.

item.title: Candidates for Minnesota governor share 'sisterhood' as cancer survivors
item.description: The rival candidates for governor of Minnesota are both breast cancer survivors, who've talked to each other about it - and spoke to a reporter about how that's shaped their lives and policies.

item.title: Texas Senate race shatters state's campaign spending record
item.description: Combined spending on advertising by Democratic state Rep. James Talarico, Republican Attorney General Ken Paxton, and super PACs supporting each of them has already topped $240 million.

item.title: New York's laws on consent and alcohol use could complicate Cornell case prosecution
item.description: NPR's Ailsa Chang talks with Erin Murphy, a professor at NYU School of Law and an expert on sexual assault law, about how New York state considers alcohol use when determining the presence of consent.

item.title: 'The Third Eye' presents an unfiltered view of the Beatles' early years
item.description: NPR's Ailsa Chang talks with Olivia Harrison about the new book The Third Eye, a collection of photographs by her late husband, George Harrison of the Beatles.

item.title: NPR spoke to Cuban men now stuck in limbo in Central African Republic
item.description: Thousands of people have been sent to countries they have no ties to and in some cases have never even heard of as part of the Trump administration's drive toward mass deportations.
